newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam sees lower trade deficit in first half.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam sees lower trade deficit in first half.

text.p: Vietnam's trade gap is likely to narrow to $1.4 billion in the first six months of this year from around $2.0 billion in the same period of 1996, a Trade Ministry official said on Wednesday.
The country posted a record trade deficit of $4.0 billion in 1996, which was equivalent to about 16 percent of its gross domestic product (GDP).
General Statistics Office figures, which are often at variance with those of the Trade Ministry, showed a trade deficit of $1.77 billion in the first six months of 1996.

The statistics office said at the end of last month that the estimated deficit for the January-May period of this year was $1.135 billion. Those figures showed a year-on-year rise of 31.8 percent in exports and just a 1.5-percent increase in imports.
Analysts say the virtually flat growth in imports reflected a slowdown in domestic investment and spending, but said the export figures were an encouraging sign.
Alarmed by a sudden ballooning of the trade deficit last year, the government has called for a push to boost export-oriented production.

The Trade Ministry official said moves were afoot to set up a state fund for export guarantees and the official Saigon Times Daily said on Wednesday that the government may launch a pilot scheme under which non-state firms would be allowed to export quota-controlled products.
However, private economists point to a recent ban on the import of certain goods as evidence that the administration is also seeking to substitute imports with domestic production.

This has raised concern that investment in import substitution today could mean difficulties for the economy tomorrow when trade liberalisation exposes those industries to fierce competition from abroad.
